sentences.text: Researchers tested male mice in a fear conditioning setup that used two different locations.

In safe areas after avoiding a threat, the animals entered a state of slow breathing and stillness, characterized by a rate of 2 to 4 times per second and hippocampal memory replay during specific brain waves.
Post-task stress levels depended on the mix of time spent freezing versus time in this slow-breathing state, rather than on the number of shocks received.
Blocking the hippocampal brain waves reduced the frequency of the slow-breathing state and increased stress, whereas administering diazepam increased the state while blocking those waves.
The authors suggest that hippocampal memory replay may help the body recover and build emotional resilience.
